headline: High-risk default write/egress overlap: Flowise can ingest and write shared files while Kestra can execute shell tasks and broad network actions, creating dangerous cross-agent data and action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise reads uploaded/server files and can run browser/tool nodes; Kestra can read/write shared files and consume stdin/stdout. If Kestra writes attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace, Flowise may treat it as trusted flow input. The pathway is plausible in default deployments, but not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem path or uploaded-file store
IF Kestra writes content that Flowise later parses as prompts or flow inputs
mitigations: Disable shared file ingestion in Flowise flows
Restrict Kestra outputs to non-executable formats
Add a manual review step before Flowise consumes Kestra-produced files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and has broad network egress; Kestra touches inputs, variables, artifacts, logs, and can send data to many external services. If they share files or datastore, sensitive chatflow data can flow into Kestra jobs and then out via APIs, creating an exfiltration path in default-capable configurations.
conditions: IF Flowise chatflow inputs or secrets are written into a shared file or datastore
IF Kestra tasks read those artifacts and forward them to external APIs or notifications
mitigations: Limit Flowise file uploads to non-sensitive data
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and audit logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and read files, and both support multiple instances. Flowise shares state via a server datastore, while Kestra can run shell tasks and broad automation. Concurrent writes to shared resources can corrupt workflows or overwrite artifacts without locking, especially if deployed against the same directory or datastore.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or database
IF concurrent runs occur without external locking or optimistic concurrency controls
mitigations: Run only one writer per datastore

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent builder that can emit tool outputs, while Kestra is an automation/orchestration system with email, Slack, cloud, and shell actions. If Kestra consumes Flowise output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Flowise result can cascade into real-world actions such as notifications, jobs, or infrastructure changes.
conditions: IF Kestra tasks use Flowise output as an input variable or trigger payload
IF those tasks perform notifications, shell commands, or cloud actions without validation
mitigations: Require human approval for actioning Flowise outputs
Log and diff Flowise outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance and confidence checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle files and logs, but Kestra explicitly touches logs, notifications, cloud storage, and multiple external services, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials. If regulated data is routed from Flowise into Kestra, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed from Flowise into Kestra workflows
IF Kestra logs, notifications, or cloud connectors retain that data longer than Flowise
mitigations: Set short retention on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
